item.description: Abstract In the modern Earth, sub-arc mantle oxygen fugacity is intrinsically associated with addition of sulfur species by slab fluids. However, it is unclear to what extent recycling of volatiles controlled redox changes of the sub-arc mantle in the early Earth. Here we use sulfur K-edge micro-X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy to measure the relative abundances of S 6+ , S 4+ and S 2− in apatite inclusions hosted by geochemically characterized and dated zircons from sub-arc sanukitoid magmas that span 3.4 billion years of Earth’s geological history. The sub-arc mantle shows marked increase in oxygen fugacity between 3.4 and 3.0 billion years ago (Ga). It is substantially more oxidized than unaltered ambient upper mantle, a characteristic that cannot be explained by fractionation, degassing or intrinsic mantle processes. We propose that progressive oxidative weathering enhanced the proportion of oxidized sulfur recycled to mantle wedge sources, establishing feedback between subduction of surface materials and incrementally oxidized arc magmatism. Early subduction involving inorganic oxidation and ‘whiffs’ of oxygen between 3.4 and 2.7 Ga may have regulated an early increase in fugacity of the sub-arc mantle before the Great Oxidation Event, matching similar conditions to the modern Earth by 2.1 Ga. item.description: Abstract The 2025 M 7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone. Our approach can inform rupture scenarios in understudied regions. Published: 2026-10-14T21:56:24+00:00 Venue: Nature Communications Score: 0.553 (flagship)

item.description: Abstract Volcanic deposits preserved within Antarctic fumarolic ice caves provide rare access to sub-ice eruptive records hidden beneath the ice cap. Here we present the first integrated textural, petrological, and geochemical characterisation of 21 tephra samples from three summit ice caves at Mount Melbourne (Northern Victoria Land, Antarctica). Major and trace-element glass compositions, combined with published datasets, were analysed using multivariate statistical workflows. Dimensionality reduction and clustering identified a distinct compositional group with no known equivalent in the existing Mount Melbourne record, suggesting that at least one previously unrecognised Holocene eruption occurred within the investigated Fumarolic Ice Caves. Correspondence between Fumarolic Ice Cave deposits and volcanic signatures in marine sediment, englacial sequences, and other proximal-distal records refined Mount Melbourne’s eruptive history and strengthened tephra correlations across archives. More broadly, sub-ice tephra archives can reveal hidden eruptive histories relevant to volcanic hazard assessment in polar regions. item.title: Deep hydrous melting of the mantle wedge recorded by Mg isotopes
item.dc:creator: Winnie X. Fan

item.description: Subduction zones govern Earth’s deep volatile cycle. The slab-mantle interface is a key locus of volatile exchange between the subducting crust and the overlying mantle wedge, yet whether and how chemical reactions at this interface affect arc magmatism remains poorly constrained. Arc magmas typically lack a geochemical hallmark of garnet fractionation, leading to the prevailing interpretation that they derive predominantly from the shallower, garnet-free mantle wedge. Here, we challenge this view using Mg isotopic data from Nicaragua, the South Sandwich Islands, and the central-eastern Aleutian arc, integrated with a global arc magma compilation. We show that heavy Mg isotopic signatures in mafic arc magmas vary with indicators of volatile enrichment, pointing to a volatile-rich source, most likely the heavily metasomatized base of the mantle wedge. The heaviest Mg isotopic compositions occur in arcs underlain by the most steeply dipping subducting slab, suggesting a focusing effect by the geometry of the downgoing slab. Monte Carlo isotope mixing models indicate that up to 50% of the Mg budget in some arc magma sources derives from deep, water-saturated melting near the slab-mantle interface. These findings highlight the base of the mantle wedge as a volumetrically and geochemically significant contributor to arc magmatism and the water cycle. item.description: Differences in lithology within alpine watersheds lead to strong contrasts in bedrock erodibility, which modulate climatic and tectonic influences on erosion, chemical weathering, and carbon dioxide exchange. However, the difficulty of measuring denudation rates in fine-grained rocks has limited our ability to quantify the magnitude of erodibility differences between weak sedimentary and strong igneous rocks. Here, we combine newly developed cosmogenic beryllium-10 measurements in shale with conventional beryllium-10 measurements in intrusive rocks, topographic analysis, solute data, and landscape evolution modeling in the East River watershed, Colorado. Shale-dominated catchments denude three times faster than adjacent intrusive catchments despite having gentler topography. Hydrochemical data and modeling indicate that elevated shale denudation enhances solute generation and net inorganic weathering–driven carbon dioxide release during prolonged landscape adjustment over million-year timescales. These results show that spatial variability in rock type alone can substantially alter the carbon dioxide balance of alpine landscapes by hiding the fastest erosion rates in relatively gentle terrain. item.description: Abstract Dark colored grassland soils, known as Mollisols, are intensively farmed and rich in organic matter, and hence have an important role in the carbon cycle. Organic carbon storage in Mollisols may result from interactions between organic matter and calcium released by carbonate and silicate weathering. Here we test this hypothesis by using a geochemical model to simulate calcium release from weathering in soils across the USA. We find that calcium released by mineral weathering is associated with soil organic carbon storage and that this effect is stronger in Mollisols than in non-Mollisols. Our model also shows that agriculture has increased calcium inputs to cultivated USA Mollisols 4-5 fold, indicating that humans have fundamentally changed the geochemical conditions that sustain organic carbon in these soils. By implication, moderating the quantity of and timing of calcium release may help to preserve and restore carbon in the world’s most intensively farmed landscapes. item.description: The origin and early radiation of winged insects (Pterygota) represent one of the most transformative events in terrestrial evolution, yet phylogenetic relationships among their basalmost lineages (Ephemeroptera, Odonata and Neoptera) continue to be a central debate within insect systematics. Here, we present the most taxonomically comprehensive phylogenomic analysis to date, leveraging genomic and transcriptomic data from 101 species, including 16 sequenced ephemeropteran genomes. Employing 1,367 universal single-copy orthologs across two supermatrices, we used concatenation- and coalescent-based frameworks under homogeneous and heterogeneous, and multispecies coalescent models. Our analyses support Palaeoptera monophyly. Although coalescent-based methods initially suggested a Chiastomyaria (Ephemeroptera + Neoptera) topology, subsequent signal dissection and topology tests confirm that the preponderance of genomic signal favors a monophyletic Palaeoptera. Furthermore, we identify incomplete lineage sorting and gene tree estimation error as the primary drivers of previous topological conflicts. Our molecular dating results point to an Early Devonian origin of crown-Pterygota, whereas crown-Palaeoptera first emerged in the Late Devonian. By reconciling molecular evidence with morphological synapomorphies, such as wing-base sclerite homologies, this study provides a coherent framework for the early evolution of winged insects, supports a single origin of wings, and identifies the neopteran wing-folding mechanism as a singular evolutionary innovation. item.title: Physics-informed deep learning links geodetic data and fault friction
item.dc:creator: Rikuto Fukushima
Masayuki Kano
Kazuro Hirahara
Makiko Ohtani
item.description: Fault slip modeling, based on laboratory-derived friction laws, has significantly enhanced our understanding of fault mechanics. Agreement between model predictions and observations supports the hypothesis that observed slip diversity, including fast earthquakes and slow transient slips (Slow Slip Events; SSEs), originates from frictional heterogeneity. However, quantitative assessments of frictional heterogeneity from geodetic observations while fully incorporating fault mechanics are lacking due to the difficulties of high-dimensional optimization. In this study, we aim to address this gap using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to link frictional heterogeneity with geodetic observations. PINNs employ a neural network to represent the spatially variable frictional properties, making their estimation feasible. Targeting the 2010 Bungo SSE in southwest Japan, our estimation reveals heterogeneous friction coinciding with localized SSE nucleation in southwest Shikoku, and subsequent westward propagation. The calculated fault slip of SSE successfully reproduces the spatio-temporal pattern of observed surface displacements. This PINN-based inversion provides a mechanically consistent fault slip model validated through quantitative comparison with observations. Furthermore, we forecast the future fault slip evolution, demonstrating the importance of assimilating observations spanning multiple SSE cycles. Our results demonstrate the potential of PINN for advancing understanding of fault mechanics and enabling physics-based fault slip forecasting. Spatially variable frictional properties along a fault can be estimated using a physics-informed neural network approach that enables physics-consistent slip modelling, as tested on the 2010 Bungo slow slip event in southwest Japan. item.description: Abstract Marine coastal systems are important for global biogeochemical cycling and are particularly sensitive to climate change effects due to their shallow depths, which results in rapid heat transfer to the sediments. Here we used one-year reciprocal in situ translocations of sediments between a Baltic Sea long-term (>50 years) warming-influenced bay and a nearby unaffected control bay to predict how the sediments and their associated bacterial communities may respond to future climate change and whether those changes were reversible. Geochemical parameters, methane plus sulfate profiles, and 16S rRNA gene-based bacterial diversity and community composition show partial convergence of the sediment-parameters to the translocated environment, suggesting climate change will rapidly alter bacteria communities of Baltic Sea coastal sediments. However, more pronounced responses in the control to the heated bay translocation direction suggest that while a return toward present-day conditions may be possible if climate change is reversed, such a recovery may be incomplete or require a longer time than one year. item.title: Onset of zircon decomposition during saprolitic weathering
item.dc:creator: Martin Yan Hei Li
Mei-Fu Zhou
item.description: Abstract Zircon is conventionally considered as refractory in supergene environments, enabling the preservation of geochemical records for tracing various Earth’s processes and the use of the zircon structure as a nuclear waste form. However, how refractory zircon is during weathering, especially when crystalline and in an early stage of weathering, is unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that crystalline zircon would start to weather during an early-stage saprolitic weathering. Nano-scale examination reveals that weathering of zircon proceeds through dissolution of primary, crystalline zircon and precipitation of secondary, amorphous zircon. Non-formula elements, like U, Th and heavy rare earth elements, are uptake and structurally incorporated in this process. Thereby, metamictisation of the zircon would accelerate and eventually promote the dissolution of zircon. In supergene environments, zircon would steadily weather, calling for further evaluation on the geological and environmental applications of zircon. item.title: Hydrogen isotopes reveal water leakage from the core
item.dc:creator: Yu Zhang
Wenzhong Wang

item.description: Chemical heterogeneities in Earth’s deep mantle may record either preserved primordial reservoirs or later core-mantle exchange, but distinguishing between these origins remains challenging. Hydrogen isotopes offer a sensitive tracer, yet whether magma ocean crystallization could generate a deuterium-depleted deep reservoir has not been quantitatively evaluated. Here, we use machine learning–accelerated path-integral simulations to determine equilibrium hydrogen isotope fractionation between silicate melt and bridgmanite, ringwoodite, and wadsleyite under magma ocean conditions. Incorporating these fractionation factors into a magma ocean crystallization model shows that mineral-melt fractionation is intrinsically weak, producing an essentially homogeneous D/H distribution in the primitive mantle. Magma ocean crystallization therefore cannot generate the extremely low δD values observed in some ocean island basalts. Combined with exceptionally high 3 He/ 4 He ratios, these signatures more plausibly reflect selective transfer of primordial volatiles from Earth’s core, implying sustained volatile exchange across the core-mantle boundary. item.description: The land-to-ocean export of carbon via rivers is a key component in the global carbon cycle. In this Review, we provide an overview of the factors governing the mobilization of carbon into rivers and those modulating riverine carbon export to the ocean. item.description: Porphyry Cu mineralization potential has long been ascribed to high magmatic oxygen fugacity, elevated volatile (H2O, Cl, S) contents, and efficient fluid migration in magma reservoirs, yet these controls lack comprehensive quantitative verification. The transition from oceanic subduction to continental collision is a key mechanism for understanding orogenic architecture and continental crustal growth. Within this framework, the geodynamic evolution of the Neo-Tethyan slab remains a subject of intensive debate concerning the formation of the Tibetan Plateau. This study presents whole-rock geochemistry and zircon U-Pb-Hf isotopes for Eocene diorite-porphyry and granite dykes from the Nyemo area, southern Lhasa subterrane. Both dyke suites were emplaced at 47–46 Ma and exhibit subduction-related arc affinities. Zircons from the diorite-porphyry and granite dykes have positive εHf(t) values of +9.0 to +11.2 and +11.9 to +13.8, respectively. The diorite-porphyry dykes exhibit high Mg#, Cr, Ni and adakitic characteristics, which indicate their derivation from partial melting of the subducted Neo-Tethyan slab followed by interaction with the overlying mantle peridotite. In contrast, the granite dykes were derived from the melting of juvenile crust and dominantly underwent fractional crystallization of K-feldspar and plagioclase. The spatiotemporal distribution of regional magmatic records, characterized by an overall eastward-younging trend, is consistent with diachronous eastward propagation of Neo-Tethyan slab breakoff. The coexistence of these two dyke suites provides evidence for slab-window development beneath the central segment of the southern Lhasa subterrane at approximately 47 Ma.

item.title: Time lag for arc volcanism following subduction initiation: A two-phase flow numerical modeling
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Zhong
Di-Cheng Zhu

item.description: Subduction initiation is a fundamental geodynamic process in plate tectonics, yet its mechanisms remain poorly understood due to the scarcity of geological records. Proposed geological records of subduction initiation, including metamorphic soles, fore-arc basalts and fore-arc sediments, are typically associated with spontaneous subduction initiation in hot environments involving mantle upwelling. In contrast, evidence for the more common cold subduction initiation at continental margins is sparse or even absent. Arc volcanic rocks are widely regarded as direct evidence of subduction zones, particularly for identifying ancient subduction zones in orogens. However, the temporal relationship between subduction initiation and the onset of arc volcanism remains poorly constrained. Although arc volcanism is generally considered to develop within ∼10 million years (Myr) of initiation, our analysis of subduction events over the past 15 Myr reveals a highly variable time lag ranging from 2 to 10 Myr. In this study, we investigate the factors controlling this time lag in forced subduction initiation at continental margins, using a newly developed two-phase flow numerical model that incorporates melt transport and melt extraction processes. Our results show that rapid partial melting at shallow depths, primarily driven by high convergence rates, leads to a shorter time lag between subduction initiation and arc volcanism, which is consistent with observations from recent subduction events. These findings suggest that arc volcanic rocks, when considered together with slab age and convergence rate, provide a useful constraint on the timing of subduction initiation in ancient subduction systems. item.description: The circum-Rodinia suprasubduction system maintained a dynamic equilibrium between extension and convergence along the periphery of the Rodinia supercontinent during its breakup. Although recent paleomagnetic data place the Yangtze Block at this margin, it remains unclear whether the Tonian tectonothermal events on its western edge are fully consistent with this configuration. This study examined a composite intrusive batholith of the Pengguan Complex on the western Yangtze margin, South China, comprising diorite, tonalite, granodiorite, biotite granite, and K-feldspar granite; however, a systematic synthesis of its properties for reconstructing the regional setting remains uncertain. Zircon U-Pb geochronology yielded consistent ages of ca. 801–794 Ma, representing the multiplex magmatic record of the western Yangtze Block during the middle Tonian. The various lithologies exhibit distinct zircon Hf-isotopic compositions, whole-rock geochemistry, Sr-Nd isotopes, and mineral geochemistry, reflecting partial melting at different levels across a continental-arc lithospheric profile. Diorite crystallized from an evolved hydrous magma ultimately related to a metasomatized mantle source, as evidenced by its arc-type trace element signatures and variable Nd-Hf isotopes. Tonalite and granodiorite display adakitic features, including elevated Sr/Y and (La/Yb)N ratios and reduced Ni and Cr concentrations, plus erratic Nd- and Hf-isotopic signatures. These features favor their derivation from partial melting of a thickened mafic lower crust. Distinct petrogenetic processes contributed to the formation of the biotite granite and K-feldspar granite, both of which are associated with transcrustal recycling. The former shows variable Nd- and Hf-isotope ratios derived from the reworking of ancient crust. In contrast, the latter has depleted Nd and Hf isotopes and younger model ages, resulting from partial melting of relatively juvenile lower-crustal components. These pieces of magmatism collectively represent multilevel partial melting of compositionally distinct domains in the mantle wedge and continental crust. The multilevel partial melting recorded by the studied batholiths in the Pengguan Complex within a continental arc setting, coupled with coeval Tonian subduction-related magmatism along the western Yangtze margin, constitutes a thermal manifestation of the convergent regime at the periphery of the Rodinia supercontinent during the early Neoproterozoic. item.description: Granite-related U deposits are generally spatially related to pre-existing granites with the crystallization ages of granites significantly earlier than the mineralization ages. The contribution of the pre-ore granitic magmatism to mineralization remains unclear. To address this issue, this study took the Lujing U deposit formed in Cretaceous–Paleogene as the research object. We carried out in situ geochronological and geochemical studies on apatite, monazite, and xenotime from the silicified fault zone, which was previously considered to be formed synchronously with mineralization, and on the zircon from the pre - existing alkali-altered granite. We discovered that the LA-ICP-MS U-Pb geochronology of the accessory minerals in the silicified fault zone and hydrothermal zircon in the granite reveals two Triassic hydrothermal activities at ∼235 Ma and ∼215 Ma, which are synchronous with regional Triassic magmatism. We therefore suggest the Triassic magmatism induced strong alkali metasomatism and the formation of silicified fault zones, which represents pre-ore, rather than syn-ore, hydrothermal activities. Mineral-element geochemistry shows that the ∼215 Ma granite has higher U concentrations than the ∼235 Ma granite. This implies that, in addition to fractional crystallization, repeated melting in the source is another important process that enhances magma fertility, as corroborated by thermodynamic modeling. The apatite from the silicified fault zone shows high Mn content (5,400–27,235 ppm), low δEu values (0.07–0.16), and high XF/XCl ratios (460–6,590). Meanwhile, the monazite from the silicified fault zone exhibits low As content (<1,000 ppm) and high Th content (99,750–207,365 ppm). The geochemical signatures indicate that the Triassic magmatic fluids were characterized by high F and low oxygen fugacity. These attributes were explained to cause the precipitation of U in the fluid via isomorphism in U-rich accessory minerals (monazite, xenotime, apatite, and uranothorite), along with minor uraninite, in granite and silicified fault zone. Therefore, we concluded that the Triassic pre-ore magmatic-hydrothermal event served as a U pre-enrichment stage for the Cretaceous–Paleogene U mineralization. This mineralization was achieved via the circulation of oxidizing fluids rich in Cl− and CO2 in Cretaceous–Paleogene, which are favorable for U dissolution. item.description: Earth’s continental crust is its most chemically evolved and diverse reservoir. Numerous studies have investigated its stable metal isotope character to understand its formation and secular evolution. Molybdenum (Mo) isotopes are useful tracers of petrogenetic processes in Phanerozoic igneous rocks, but Archean granitoids, which make up much of Earth’s early continental crust, remain poorly characterized. Here, we report high-precision whole-rock Mo isotope data for 28 Archean granitoids from Australia’s Pilbara and Yilgarn cratons, with crystallization ages from 3.52 to 2.63 Ga. The samples cover a spectrum of magmatic series, including tonalite-trondhjemite-granodiorite (TTG), TTG hybrid, sanukitoid, potassic, and potassic hybrid magmas. After assessing the effects of alteration, crustal contamination, and fluid exsolution, we interpret the observed δ 98/95Mo range of − 0.93 to 0.25‰ as primarily reflecting magmatic source characteristics. TTG and TTG hybrid granitoids, together with samples derived from unenriched meta-mafic or mantle-like sources, have mean and median δ 98/95Mo values close to, or slightly higher than, chondrite and depleted MORB mantle (DMM). In contrast, potassic, potassic hybrid, and sanukitoid series granitoids, as well as samples derived from enriched meta-mafic or felsic crustal sources, extend to lower, sub-mantle δ 98/95Mo values. Elemental proxy relationships, major- and trace-element modeling, and phase-equilibrium constraints indicate that source composition and residual mineralogy during partial melting primarily control Mo isotope variability in these rocks. In crustally-derived granitoids, lower δ 98/95Mo values are associated with more mature source compositions and with changes in the abundance and composition of residual feldspar. Amphibole, garnet, and biotite may also have subordinate effects. These relationships suggest that Mo isotopes track the progressive reworking of Archean crust. Juvenile crust-derived TTG magmatism is characterized by near- to suprachondritic δ 98/95Mo, whereas later sanukitoid and potassic granitoid magmatism, linked respectively to mantle metasomatism and reworking of TTG-dominated gray gneiss, shifts toward lower δ 98/95Mo values. The observed trends imply that intracrustal reworking alone can push continental averages to sub-mantle values, with ramifications for mass-balance models. Although TTGs are generally suprachondritic, their δ 98/95Mo values are not high enough to easily support models requiring large volumes of Hadean to Paleoarchean continental extraction from a chondritic mantle to offset the subchondritic Mo isotope composition inferred for the depleted mantle from Archean komatiites. The strong Mo isotope contrast between continental crust and upper mantle may therefore have developed after 2.6 Ga, once crustal recycling became more extensive. item.title: Subduction Recycling and Closure of the Paleo‐Asian Ocean in the Beishan Orogen: Constraints From the Niujuanzi Ophiolitic Mélange and Associated Intrusions

item.description: Abstract Ophiolitic mélanges and associated intrusions provide key archives for reconstructing the evolution of ancient ocean basins and subduction‐related mantle modification. The Hongliuhe–Niujuanzi–Xichangjing ophiolitic mélange in the central Beishan Orogen preserves important records of the Paleo‐Asian Ocean, but the timing of oceanic subduction, terminal closure, and subsequent postcollisional reworking in the Niujuanzi remain debated. Here we integrate field observations, zircon U–Pb geochronology, whole‐rock and mineral geochemistry, and Sr–Nd–Hf–Pb isotopic data from the newly dated and geochemically characterized ophiolitic rocks and associated dioritic to granodioritic intrusions. Zircon U–Pb ages define three Paleozoic magmatic episodes: Early Silurian diorites at 435–427 Ma, Late Silurian ophiolitic gabbros at 423–418 Ma, and Early Devonian granodiorites at ca. 403 Ma. The diorites display continental arc‐like geochemical signatures and were derived from a lithospheric mantle source modified by slab‐derived fluids. The gabbros show N‐MORB‐like affinities with weak subduction‐related enrichment, consistent with formation in an SSZ setting. The granodiorites were generated mainly by partial melting of the ancient lower crust with minor mantle input, recording a transition to postcollisional extension. Silicate in situ Pb isotopes exhibit a temporal shift toward Indian MORB‐like signatures from the Early Silurian to Early Devonian, indicating progressive mantle source modification by recycled subduction components. These results demonstrate that the Niujuanzi basin remained active until the Late Silurian, closed by the end‐Silurian, closed during the latest Silurian to the earliest Devonian (ca. 418 Ma), and transitioned to postcollisional extension in the Early Devonian, providing a refined geodynamic model for the central Beishan Orogen. item.description: Kimberlites and related CO2-rich ultramafic rocks such as aillikites commonly show Nd-Hf isotope decoupling (unradiogenic εHf at a given εNd), attributed to either recycled oceanic slabs or interaction with metasomatized continental lithospheric mantle (CLM). We present potassium isotope data (δ41K) for Neoproterozoic aillikites from West Greenland and use δ41K-ε176Hf covariations to test these models. Aillikite δ41K ranges from −0.62‰ to −0.31‰ and correlates positively with εHf, indicating mixing between distinct mantle reservoirs rather than magmatic differentiation. The data can be reproduced by mixing a K-poor, high-δ41K carbonatitic melt with a K-rich, low-δ41K CLM metasome characterized by unradiogenic Hf. We infer a two-stage evolution in which CO2-rich melts formed in the asthenosphere from domains containing recycled carbonate-rich oceanic material and then acquired their potassic compositions and decoupled Nd-Hf isotope signatures during ascent through heterogeneous CLM. item.description: The Socorro-Guaxupé Thrust Nappe (SGTN) is a metamorphic high-grade allochthonous terrane situated in southeast Brazil, interpreted as a segment of a Late Neoproterozoic magmatic arc that developed along the margin of a continental plate. item.description: The surface nitrogen (N) cycle is dominated by biological activity, yet its impact on the deep N cycle is poorly constrained. item.description: The bedrock of Jutulsessen, central Dronning Maud Land (East Antarctica), comprises orthogneisses and migmatites interlayered with mafic and pelitic granulites of the Mesoproterozoic Maud Belt. These rocks record high-grade metamorphism associated with the Ediacaran–Cambrian orogeny during the assembly of Gondwana. Here, we reconstruct the pressure-temperature (P–T) evolution of the granulites using mineral assemblages, inclusion suites, reaction textures, and phase equilibria (pseudosection) modelling. The granulites record a clockwise P–T path, which involves prograde burial to high-pressure granulite-facies conditions, followed by decompression at elevated temperatures and subsequent cooling and hydration at lower-grade conditions. Garnet growth is associated with amphibolite- to granulite-facies inclusion assemblages. Peak-pressure conditions are preserved in low-strain mafic lenses containing the assemblage garnet + clinopyroxene + quartz + plagioclase, and by the occurrence of kyanite + rutile in pelitic rocks. Garnet-breakdown textures in mafic rocks and the transformation of kyanite-bearing assemblages to sillimanite- and cordierite-bearing assemblages in pelitic rocks record high-temperature decompression. Microtextures in the pelitic granulites indicate that decompression was locally accompanied by partial melting, resulting in garnet breakdown and regrowth linked to melt production. Retrograde cooling is reflected by clinopyroxene exsolution and fluid-assisted amphibole growth in mafic rocks, as well as by biotite growth in supracrustal rocks. The reconstructed P–T path records crustal thickening and deep burial, followed by high-temperature decompression and exhumation, consistent with tectonic models for the Ediacaran–Cambrian assembly of Gondwana. item.description: Abstract We present BaSIC: Basalt Source Investigation and Characterization, an open‐source Python based Bayesian inversion method to constrain the source mineralogy of basalts. item.description: Over the past billion years, Earth’s large-scale tectonics have been dominated by the assembly and breakup of supercontinents Rodinia and Pangea. Yet, previous geodynamic simulations predicted that whole mantle convection would stabilize in a fixed, long-wavelength mode, with a common degree-1 pattern resembling a stable supercontinent. In contrast, geological records show that continental arcs rapidly formed along circum-supercontinent passive margins shortly prior to the breakup of Rodinia and Pangea, indicating successful subduction initiation and an evolving supercontinent cycle. Thus, it requires an additional mechanism for subduction initiation along circum-supercontinent passive margins beyond self-organizing mantle flow. Here, we propose a new mechanism for subduction initiation at the passive margin before supercontinent breakup, based on geological records and the recent finding that the cratonic lithospheric mantle comprises a buoyant upper layer, a weak mid-lithospheric discontinuity, and a dense lower layer. We demonstrate that perturbations, such as plume underplating or melt infiltration, could initiate delamination of the dense lower cratonic mantle lithosphere, while the remaining buoyant continent uplifts, weakening the nearby passive margin and decoupling the continental and oceanic lithosphere. Eventually, the enhanced density contrast across the former passive margin leads to the formation of a new ocean-continent subduction zone. We suggest that this new subduction initiation mechanism is a key driver of the periodic operation of supercontinent cycles, modulating Earth’s long-term tectonic evolution. item.title: Development of Arsenopyrite Reference Materials (Sacra and Niko) for In situ Multiple Sulfur Isotope Measurement

item.description: Advances in high‐resolution in situ techniques, such as SIMS and LA‐ICP‐MS, now enable precise multiple sulfur isotope measurements at spatial resolutions of tens of micrometres, providing new insights into redox evolution, metal behaviour and fluid pathways in ore‐forming systems. The accuracy of the measurement results depends critically on the availability of matrix‐matched reference materials, which have not yet been developed for arsenopyrite. To address this gap, we introduce two new arsenopyrite reference materials, Niko and Sacra. Bulk isotope ratio mass spectrometry analyses yield mean compositions of δ 33 S = +2.28 ± 0.01‰, δ 34 S = +4.44 ± 0.04‰, Δ 33 S = ‐0.002 ± 0.009‰, Δ 36 S = ‐0.142 ± 0.342‰ for Niko, and δ 33 S = +0.38 ± 0.07‰, δ 34 S = +0.76 ± 0.14‰, Δ 33 S = ‐0.007 ± 0.003‰, Δ 36 S = ‐0.275 ± 0.185‰ for Sacra. All uncertainties are reported as 2 s of replicate bulk analyses (Niko n = 3; Sacra n = 3). SIMS analyses showed lower measurement repeatability for Niko (δ 34 S = 0.39‰, and Δ 33 S = 0.151‰; 2 s , n = 35) as compared with Sacra (0.98‰ and Δ 33 S = 0.330‰, 2 s , n = 44). These results support the use of Niko as a primary matrix‐matched reference material for in situ multiple sulfur isotope measurement, with Sacra serving as a secondary reference and quality control material. The applicability of Niko and Sacra is currently validated for arsenopyrite compositions within or close to the compositional range represented by these two materials; the effects of more extreme variations in S/As ratio and Fe abundance on matrix‐dependent instrumental mass fractionation remain to be evaluated. Niko and Sacra therefore provide new matrix‐matched materials for improving the reproducibility of in situ multiple sulfur isotope analyses of near‐stoichiometric arsenopyrite, thereby strengthening SIMS‐based investigations of sulfur cycling and ore‐forming processes.
